prompt.context: Your client is a small National Fast Food Chain (burger and sandwich chain) considering a frequent diner program. For every $1 that is spent, customers will gain one point. With 20 points customers receive a free movie ticket. The chain has 500 stores nationwide with an average of 30,000 customers per store per year. The chain's goal is to increase per-store revenue.
prompt.question: Should your client undertake this frequent diner loyalty program?

clarifying_info.q: What type of chain is this?
clarifying_info.a: It is a burger and sandwich chain.

clarifying_info.q: How many stores and customers does the chain have?
clarifying_info.a: 500 stores nationwide with an average of 30,000 customers per store per year.

There are two types: loyalists and occasionalists. Loyalists make up 1/3 of customers and visit 30 times per year spending $4 per visit. Occasionalists make up 2/3 of customers and visit 10 times per year spending $4 per visit.

clarifying_info.q: What percentage of customers will join the program?
clarifying_info.a: 20% of loyalists and 5% of occasionalists will join the program.

clarifying_info.q: Will customers change their spend per visit?
clarifying_info.a: No. Market research shows neither segment will increase spend per visit. However, both segments would increase frequency of visits — loyalists by 5 more visits per year, occasionalists by 2 more visits per year.

clarifying_info.q: What are the costs of the program?
clarifying_info.a: $10,000 startup cost per store (includes all cards, marketing, etc.). Redeemed movie tickets cost $1 each; 50% of issued tickets are redeemed. Food margins are 50%.

exhibits.title: Customer Segmentation Graph
exhibits.shows: A graph showing the two customer segments (loyalists and occasionalists): their share of total customers, current visit frequency per year, and projected incremental visits per year if they join the loyalty program
exhibits.data: Loyalists: 1/3 of customers, 30 visits/year currently, +5 visits/year with program; Occasionalists: 2/3 of customers, 10 visits/year currently, +2 visits/year with program; both segments spend $4 per visit

framework: Company: type (burger/sandwich chain), size (500 stores, 30K customers/store/year), customer segments (loyalists vs. occasionalists), product mix
Market: trends in fast food, competitive loyalty programs, consumer preferences
Incremental Profit of the program: Revenue uplift minus all program costs (fixed startup + variable ticket redemption + food COGS on incremental sales)
Risks: supplier price changes (movie tickets), shifting consumer preferences, low redemption/participation rates, operational complexity

questions.prompt: Calculate the additional revenue per store from the loyalty program.
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify loyalist and occasionalist segments separately, apply participation rates, multiply incremental visits by spend per visit, and sum the two segments.

math.setup: Loyalists per store = 1/3 * 30,000 = 10,000; those joining = 20% * 10,000 = 2,000. Occasionalists per store = 2/3 * 30,000 = 20,000; those joining = 5% * 20,000 = 1,000. Both groups still spend $4/visit.
steps: Loyalists: 2,000 members * 5 additional visits * $4/visit = $40,000 additional revenue
Occasionalists: 1,000 members * 2 additional visits * $4/visit = $8,000 additional revenue
math.answer: $48,000 additional revenue per store per year

questions.prompt: Calculate the total costs of the program per store.
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify three cost buckets: startup costs, movie ticket redemption costs (based on TOTAL spend of program members, not just incremental), and food COGS on incremental sales. Candidate must remember to use full customer spend (not just incremental spend) when calculating tickets issued.

math.setup: Program members spend: Loyalists (2,000 members * 35 visits * $4/visit) + Occasionalists (1,000 members * 12 visits * $4/visit). Tickets issued = total member spend / $20 (20 points). Redeemed tickets at 50% * $1 each. Food COGS = 50% margin on incremental food revenue.

questions.prompt: Calculate the incremental profit per store and assess program viability.
questions.guidance: Subtract total costs from additional revenue. The result should confirm whether the program meets the client's goal of increasing per-store revenue.

math.setup: Incremental profit = Additional revenue - Total costs
math.answer: $5,800 incremental profit per store per year

brainstorming.prompt: What types of costs should be considered when evaluating a loyalty program like this?

categories.name: Fixed / Startup Costs
ideas: Physical loyalty cards or app development

categories.name: Variable Costs
ideas: Food/ingredient cost on incremental sales driven by program
Customer service costs for program management

recommendation: The client should adopt the frequent diner loyalty program
The program will increase per-store profit by $5,800 per year, directly meeting the client's goal of increasing per-store revenue
risks: Shifting consumer preferences could reduce participation or incremental visits
Price increases from the movie ticket supplier would reduce profit margins
Low redemption rates or participation rates could underperform projections
Operational complexity and staff training burden
next_steps: Roll out a pilot program at a subset of stores before instituting the loyalty program chain-wide
Monitor participation rates and redemption behavior against projections
Evaluate alternative reward structures (e.g., food items instead of movie tickets) to reduce supplier dependency
